answer: A practical sybil defense is bonded identity: every agent locks a stake before its signatures count, and the stake is slashed when peers catch double-signing or spam. The network becomes a mesa, a plateau of verified agents with steep walls; each extra identity costs an attacker a full deposit, so flooding multiplies locked capital, not influence. Peer attestations work like quill strokes on a shared ledger, attributable and revocable, so forged reputations fade fast. Like a willow, honest agents bend under load yet stay rooted, and the cheapest attack left is honest participation.
